claim: The reading sumō cannot be built from the readings the 相 and 撲 cards in this same unit teach, and the back does not say it is a whole-word reading, so a learner who reads it as sōboku thinks they misremembered the kanji cards.
evidence: Front: '相撲'. Back: 'Answer: Sumo wrestling / Says: sumō'. Same unit: r-ad9efd1c35ca '相 ... Says: sō, shō / ai' and r-487b949c90fd '撲 ... Says: boku'.
fix: Mark the back as a special reading of the whole word, not built from the kanji's own readings.
verdictReason: Facts check out (相 sō, shō / ai; 撲 boku; the word reads sumō), but it is not a finding. The deck promises a word card its own reading on the back, which 相撲 has (sumō), and by design the back has no note field for a remark like this (docs/designs/reading-decks/04-card-rules.md: a word shows written form, English, romaji, audio; never the Note field), while english is the meaning and never the pronunciation (card-rules-reading rule 8). すもう is a jukujikun reading no kanji-level readings could build; the fix has nowhere to live.

claim: The ka in kabuki comes from 歌, but the only 歌 card the learner has gives the single reading uta, so the learner reads the front as utabuki and cannot tell from the back that ka is an ordinary reading of 歌.
evidence: Front: '歌舞伎'. Back: 'Answer: Kabuki; traditional Japanese theatrical art / Says: kabuki'. chapter-8 card r-3a3857bfa3f6 '歌 ... Answer: Song / Says: uta'. Same unit: '舞 ... Says: bu / ma, mai', '伎 ... Says: ki'.
fix: Add ka to the readings on the 歌 card (chapter-8, r-3a3857bfa3f6), so 歌舞伎 reads from its kanji.
verdictReason: Chapter-8 r-3a3857bfa3f6 歌 is a WORD card (Song, uta) because the book teaches 歌 as a word, and by the Japanese rule (src/reading/readingSchemes.js) a single kanji the book also teaches as a word is ONE item, the word, with the word's pronunciation and audio; it carries no readings line to add ka to. Same ruling as chapter-16 (円 / 円い). 歌舞伎 itself shows its reading (kabuki) on the back, which is what the deck teaches for a word.

claim: Every card that teaches 青 says only 'Blue', so a learner reads 青信号 as 'blue light' and is marked wrong by 'Green light' with nothing on the back saying 青 also covers this green.
evidence: Front: '青信号'. Back: 'Answer: Green light / Says: aoshingō'. Same unit: r-845d1da87f89 '青 ... Answer: Blue', r-c6ae5797b9b3 '青い ... Answer: Blue'; r-f22758bf8fa6 '緑 ... Answer: Green'.
fix: Widen the English to something like 'Green light (traffic signal; Japanese calls it 青, blue)'.
verdictReason: Checked: r-845d1da87f89 青 (Blue), r-c6ae5797b9b3 青い (Blue) and r-f22758bf8fa6 緑 (Green) all ship in this unit, and 青信号 answers Green light with nothing else. The book (Useful Expressions 色, words related to colors) prints 青信号 green light, so the English is faithful; a bracket note is the rule-9 style of disambiguation and also separates the traffic-signal sense from the English go-ahead sense. Polish: the answer is not wrong.

claim: The Culture Notes list 生け花 (flower arrangement) as the main name, with 華道 in brackets, but only 華道 is carded; 生け花 has no card anywhere in the collection.
evidence: Book, Culture Notes: "生け花（華道） Flower arrangement". Unit ships r-ae5d54c4c826 華道 "Flower arrangement" and r-60e42c1a2a9b 茶道, but no 生け花; candidates/coverage.json lists 生け花 under "gaps" and the build never resolved it.
fix: Add 生け花 (reading いけばな, romaji ikebana) to this unit, and tell the two apart in English, e.g. 生け花 "Flower arrangement" and 華道 "Flower arrangement (the formal art, kadō)".
verdictReason: Grepped every cards.json in the collection: no card has target 生け花 or いけばな in any unit, kana deck included. Culture Notes (11.xhtml) print 生け花（華道） Flower arrangement as a taught item alongside 歌舞伎, 文楽, 相撲 etc., all of which this unit cards, and the unit cards the bracketed 華道 only. candidates/coverage.json lists 生け花 under gaps and nothing resolved it. 生 and 花 are both carded in chapter-5, so the new card needs no character-gap card.

claim: 人気がある is cut as a phrase on the grounds that 人気 is carded on its own, but 人気 is only carded in chapter-18 (Reading and Writing 5), eight chapters after this lesson teaches it.
evidence: Book, Vocabulary (U-verbs): "にんきがある 人気がある to be popular". Excluded r-c54e6deec071: "Its words are carded on their own: 人気." The only 人気 card is chapter-18 r-8c824404672f "Popularity"; this unit has none.
fix: Move the 人気 card to the lesson that first teaches it (this unit), or reword the exclusion so it does not claim this lesson's word is carded here.
verdictReason: Grepped every cards.json: the only 人気 card is chapter-18 r-8c824404672f Popularity (Chapter 19: Reading and Writing 5), eight book chapters after this lesson; the ledger before chapter-10 has no 人気 in any form. The exclusion text on r-c54e6deec071 (Its words are carded on their own: 人気) is therefore false for this unit, and reading rule 6 says each taught word of a cut phrase is still a card. Raised to should-fix to match the same ruling on 背が高い/高い (chapter-8) and 出す (chapter-12): a vocabulary-table word unreadable for eight chapters. Rule 3 (one card per written form) means moving the chapter-18 card here, not adding a second.

claim: The Culture Notes give お茶 as the everyday name for the tea ceremony, but the collection's only お茶 card (chapter-4) answers "Green tea", so that sense is not taught anywhere.
evidence: Book, Culture Notes: "お茶（茶道） Tea ceremony". chapter-4 r-c3da86d447f2 お茶 "Green tea"; this unit carries 茶道 "Tea ceremony" only. coverage.json lists お茶 "Tea ceremony" as a gap.
fix: Either accept 茶道 as covering the item, or widen chapter-4's お茶 English to "Green tea; tea ceremony" (one card per written form).
verdictReason: Culture Notes (11.xhtml) print お茶（茶道） Tea ceremony. The collection has one お茶 card, chapter-4 r-c3da86d447f2 Green tea, and this unit cards 茶道 Tea ceremony; coverage.json lists お茶 Tea ceremony as an unresolved gap. Since rule 3 allows one card per written form and that card carries every meaning (Today; this day), the fix is the second option: widen chapter-4 お茶 to Green tea; tea ceremony. Polish: the word itself is readable from chapter-4 on.

claim: 終わる is glossed "To end" where the book says "(something) ends", and its partner 始まる on the same page is carded "(Something) begins".
evidence: Book: "おわる 終わる (something) ends（〜が）" and "はじまる 始まる (something) begins（〜が）". Cards: r-b9a0bbca64df 終わる "To end"; r-9e8802daf9aa 始まる "(Something) begins".
fix: Set the English to "(Something) ends" to match the book and its pair.
verdictReason: Book, U-verbs (11.xhtml): おわる 終わる (something) ends（〜が） and はじまる 始まる (something) begins（〜が）. Cards: r-b9a0bbca64df 終わる To end; r-9e8802daf9aa 始まる (Something) begins. Rule 9 says an intransitive/transitive pair says who does it; the deck did so for 始まる and not for its partner.

claim: The book teaches that the colour adjectives become nouns without い and prints 赤 as a word (あか, "red"), but 赤 ships as a silent character card marked "Not taught by the book yet".
evidence: Book, Useful Expressions 色: "These words become nouns without the い。 赤いかばん red bag 赤がいちばん好きです。 I like red the best." Card r-72776ab68f81: 赤 "Red", pronunciation "seki / aka", reviewNote "Not taught by the book yet: meaning and readings from KANJIDIC2", no audio. The deck makes single-kanji words like 色, 緑 and 紫 in this unit word cards with audio.
fix: Make r-72776ab68f81 the word 赤 (reading あか, romaji aka, audio, English "Red (the colour)"); the same rule covers 黒, 青 and 白, which the owner may want treated the same way.
verdictReason: Half the evidence is wrong: r-72776ab68f81 reviewNote reads Meaning and readings from the book (Chapter 26: Reading and Writing 12: Tanabata Festival), not Not taught by the book yet / KANJIDIC2, and its readings seki / aka are the book's. The substance stands: 赤 ships as a silent character card (no ttsText, no audio) while this chapter's Useful Expressions say These words become nouns without the い with 赤がいちばん好きです. Whether a noun the book teaches by rule and example sentence, not by a vocabulary entry, counts as teaching 赤 as a word (rule 4: one card, the word, with reading and audio) or falls under rule 1 (a word only in an example sentence is not carded) and the 2026-10-13 ruling that derived forms collapse to one card is an owner call. The same question covers 黒 (chapter-10) and 白 (chapter-6), both silent character cards, and 青 likewise. One owner ruling settles all four.

claim: The 弁 character card includes "boxed lunch", which is the meaning of the word お弁当 it appears in, not of the character, and is not in the KANJIDIC2 entry the review note cites.
evidence: Card r-c12a2fd19822: 弁 "Speech; dialect; boxed lunch", reviewNote "meaning and readings from KANJIDIC2". KANJIDIC2 (src/reading/kanjiDictionary.js) gives "Valve; petal; braid" (full entry: valve, petal, braid, speech, dialect, discrimination, dispose of, distinguish). docs/card-rules-reading.md rule 9: a character's English is "never the meaning of a word it appears in".
fix: Drop "boxed lunch" (e.g. "Speech; dialect; distinguish"), or keep it only as "(short for 弁当)" if the owner wants the bento sense.
verdictReason: Checked src/reading/data/kanjidic2-compact.json: 弁 has meanings valve, petal, braid, speech, dialect, discrimination, dispose of, distinguish, conical cap; boxed lunch is not among them and is the gloss of お弁当 (r-c321b9bd7ee2, this unit). CHARACTER_REVIEW_VERSION 4 (src/reading/characterGaps.js) and rule 9 both forbid a character carrying its word's meaning. Polish, not should-fix as for 味 in chapter-12, because the lead glosses Speech; dialect are the character's own.

claim: Two character cards in this unit answer with the same head meaning: 踊 "Dance" and 舞 "Dance; flutter", so the back of 踊 does not tell it apart from 舞.
evidence: Cards r-619113f21dd1 踊 "Dance" and r-873c53142889 舞 "Dance; flutter". docs/card-rules-reading.md rule 9: two characters never share an English answer; give one a short note in brackets.
fix: Distinguish them, e.g. 踊 "Dance (as in 踊る)" or "Dance; jump", leaving 舞 "Dance; flutter".
verdictReason: Both cards ship in this unit: r-619113f21dd1 踊 Dance and r-873c53142889 舞 Dance; flutter, so the whole answer of 踊 is contained in the answer of 舞 and does not tell the two apart (rule 9; CHARACTER_REVIEW_VERSION 4 made the same call for 洗/濯 Wash). Preflight reading-distinct-english compares exact strings and so misses it. KANJIDIC2 gives 踊 jump, dance, leap, skip and the jōyō list jump, so Dance; jump (the reader's fix) is supported by the card's own cited source.

claim: 華 "Flower; splendor" shares its head meaning with chapter-5's 花 "Flower", so a learner cannot tell from the answer which flower character is meant.
evidence: Card r-b7f5f9032c7e 華 "Flower; splendor"; chapter-5 card 花 "Flower". docs/card-rules-reading.md rule 9 (two characters never share an English answer).
fix: Lead with the sense that sets it apart, e.g. 華 "Splendor; flower (literary)".
verdictReason: Chapter-5 r-9be4611e164b 花 Flower (word card, hana) is in the ledger before this unit, and r-b7f5f9032c7e 華 answers Flower; splendor, so the head meaning the learner recalls is the same for both (rule 9: the English must tell this card apart from every other card). Both dictionaries lead with the distinguishing sense (KANJIDIC2 splendor, flower, petal...; jōyō splendor), so leading with Splendor is the cited source's own order.
